newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Casualties mount as Sri Lanka troops resume advance.
newsitem.headline: Casualties mount as Sri Lanka troops resume advance.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops pushed deeper into the Tamil rebels' northern heartland on Friday after consolidating their hold on a rebel town captured two days ago, military officials in the north said.

Troops, backed by tanks, artillery and air cover, rolled out of Omanthai, 14 km (nine miles) north of Vavuniya, on Friday afternoon, heading towards the heavily fortified rebel-held town of Puliyankulam further north, they said.
"Troops have advanced about two kms (1.2 miles) from Omanthai. They are being met by stiff resistance from the rebels," one official told Reuters.

A pitched battle was being fought near Nedunkeni, about 40 km (25 miles) northeast of Vavuniya, where troops advancing along an eastern flanks were being attacked by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), other officials said.
The LTTE's international spokesman in London said he was unaware of fighting in Nedunkeni, where several key rebel camps are located.

"Nedunkeni, which is far away from the army's advance, is being pounded by the military from the air. Thousands of civilians residing there have been forced to flee," Anton Raja told Reuters by telephone.

At least 28 rebels, including four women cadres, were killed on the fourth day of fighting after the military launched a major offensive into the rebel-controlled Wanni region on Tuesday, military officials said.

Troops based in Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo, backed by artillery, tanks and helicopter gunships, launched the offensive code-named "Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", on Tuesday.
The Defence Ministry on Friday said nine soldiers were killed and eight wounded during the past 24 hours, bringing the official military death toll to 27 and those wounded to 31.
Military sources in the north said about 80 soldiers had been wounded since the offensive began, some of them seriously.
The Defence Ministry said on Thursday that troops monitoring LTTE transmissions confirmed that at least 100 rebels had been killed or wounded in the battle for Omanthai alone.
But the clandestine rebel Voice of Tiger radio, monitored in Vavuniya, said on Friday the LTTE had lost only six people in the four days of fighting. It did not say how many were wounded.

The Defence Ministry says the main aim of the drive is to capture areas in the shrub-covered Wanni region from the LTTE, who are waging a war for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east.
Analysts said the offensive aims to open a land supply route linking Vavuniya in north-central Sri Lanka with the Jaffna peninsula, about 100 km (60 miles) further north.
The military has been tight-lipped about where the troops are heading.
The LTTE's Raja on Friday accused the military of killing Tamil civilians and destroying their property under the guise of opening up a supply route.
"The people are on the run again," he said. "They are moving into the jungles for safety. It is raining in the Wanni and they are without food and shelter."
An international aid worker in Vavuniya told Reuters at least 10 civilians had been killed and more wounded in the artillery shelling of the Wanni.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the toll is higher.
